title: HIRU Launches Cycling Shorts With a Menstrual Chamois Built for Women Who Ride, Period.
content:
Chamois design has gotten pretty nerdy over the years. We’ve got multi-density foams, perforations, crazy shapes, and even the KuKu Penthouse from Assos. Somehow, though, the idea of building one for riding during your period has been left behind. Unfortunately, it’s not totally surprising in this industry. Thankfully, HIRU, Orbea’s cycling apparel brand, is stepping in with its first shorts that feature a menstrual chamois. Meet the HIRU Menstrual Chamois Shorts.

The new shorts are the result of two years of development. HIRU built multiple prototypes and tested them in the real world with female cyclists, aiming for a chamois suited to period days that still holds up to long-distance riding, training, and racing. As HIRU’s Product Director Óscar Pérez puts it, “If it’s that week, it’s still your week.”

But How Does it Work?

The big change is in the textile technology. The chamois uses targeted absorbent zones to capture fluid and keep the surface dry and comfortable. An integrated technical membrane acts as a barrier against leaks. All while still keeping the padded properties you need to sit on a saddle for hours on end. In HIRU’s development testing, the chamois absorbed up to 30 ml of fluid in one minute. The polyester surface also gets an anti-odour treatment.

The Chamois Tech

Under all that, the padding still gets the full chamois treatment. There are three foam layers, and each has a job: a 4 mm elastic memory foam, a 6 mm reticulated foam rated at 140 kPa, and a high-impact foam at 65 kPa. Together, they’re meant to dampen vibration and keep things comfortable late in a long day. HIRU says the result is a chamois that keeps the comfort and light weight it’s been known for.

HIRU Menstrual Chamois Shorts Retail & Detail

Retail: TBD

  • Absorbency: Up to 30 ml in one minute (HIRU’s development testing)
  • Absorption design: Targeted absorbent zones to capture fluid and keep the surface dry
  • Leak protection: Integrated technical membrane barrier
  • Odour control: Anti-odour treatment on the polyester surface
  • Foam layer 1: 4 mm elastic memory foam
  • Foam layer 2: 6 mm reticulated foam, 140 kPa
  • Foam layer 3: High-impact foam, 65 kPa
  • Intended use: Long-distance riding, training, and racing
  • Development: Two years, multiple prototypes, real-world testing with women cyclists
  • Versions: Short and long
  • Colors: Short in pink or black; long in burgundy or black

The shorts come in both short and long versions to cover different conditions and rider preferences. The short version comes in pink or black, and the long version in burgundy or black.

It’s a straightforward idea executed with the same foam-spec attention we’d expect from any high-end pad. We’ll be curious to hear how the absorbency and leak protection hold up over long days on the bike.

The shorts are on sale now through HIRU’s usual channels, including specialist retailers and the Orbea website. Hit the link below for more info.
